ap_psychology-m01.stem: Participants watch a short video of a minor traffic accident. Half are asked how fast the cars were going when they 'smashed' into each other, and half are asked how fast the cars were going when they 'bumped' into each other. A week later, all are asked whether there was broken glass in the video. What is the independent variable?

options.text: The video of the accident
options.why: All participants saw the same video, so it is held constant.

options.text: The participants' reports about broken glass
options.why: Reports about broken glass are the dependent variable.

options.text: The one-week delay
options.why: The delay was the same for everyone, so it is held constant.

options.text: The verb used in the question about speed
options.why: The researchers manipulated the wording of the question that participants were asked.

ap_psychology-m01.stem: In the accident study, the researchers randomly assigned participants to the two question wordings. Why is this useful for the researchers' conclusion?

options.text: It ensures that all participants remember the video equally well
options.why: Random assignment does not equalize memory for the video.

options.text: It makes the groups similar before the manipulation, so differences in later reports are more likely due to the wording.
options.why: Random assignment helps control preexisting differences between groups.

options.text: It prevents participants from knowing the purpose of the study
options.why: Random assignment does not hide the purpose from participants.

options.text: It allows the researchers to generalize to all witnesses of accidents
options.why: Generalization depends on how participants were sampled.

ap_psychology-m02.stem: A teacher tests whether flashcards help memory more than rereading notes. Students who chose flashcards studied in the morning, and students who chose rereading studied late at night; the flashcard group then scored higher on a quiz. Which variable most directly threatens the conclusion that flashcards caused the higher scores?

options.text: The dependent variable of quiz score
options.why: The quiz score is the outcome being measured, not a confound.

options.text: Time of day of studying
options.why: Time of day differed between the groups along with the study method, so it is a confound.

options.text: The number of quiz questions
options.why: All students answered the same quiz, so the number of questions did not vary between groups.

options.text: The students' enjoyment of the teacher
options.why: Nothing in the description suggests that enjoyment differed between groups.

ap_psychology-m03.stem: A school gives the same student the same vocabulary test twice, one week apart, and gets scores of 62 and 91. Which quality of the test is most clearly in question?

options.text: Standardization
options.why: Standardization concerns uniform procedures and norms for a test.

options.text: Reliability
options.why: A test that gives very different scores to the same person under similar conditions lacks reliability.

options.text: Validity
options.why: Validity concerns whether the test measures what it is intended to measure.

options.text: Predictive power for achievement
options.why: Predictive power is evaluated by comparing scores with later outcomes.

ap_psychology-m03.stem: A company develops a test of creativity and finds that scores on the test are nearly the same when students take it twice. However, the scores are unrelated to any other measure of creative work. Which statement best describes the test?

options.text: It is neither reliable nor standardized.
options.why: The consistent scores indicate reliability.

options.text: It is reliable and therefore valid.
options.why: Reliability does not guarantee validity.

options.text: It appears reliable but its validity is in doubt.
options.why: Consistent scores show reliability, but unrelated results suggest the test may not measure creativity.

options.text: It is valid but not reliable.
options.why: Validity requires consistency, and here the scores are consistent.

ap_psychology-m04.stem: A test of musical aptitude was normed on students from one city. Researchers discover that students from other cultures score lower even when they play instruments equally well. Which concern does this raise about the test?

options.text: The test measures intelligence rather than aptitude
options.why: The scenario does not indicate that the test measures intelligence.

options.text: The test is not standardized, because it was normed in a city
options.why: Norming on a group is part of standardization; the concern is that the norm group may not represent others.

options.text: Possible test bias
options.why: Group differences unrelated to the ability being measured raise concerns of test bias.

options.text: The test must have high reliability
options.why: Differences between groups do not show that reliability is high.

ap_psychology-m05.stem: In the retrieval practice study, students in the quiz group scored 18 percentage points higher on a final test than students who reread notes. options.text: Reporting the difference in percentage points
options.why: How a difference is reported does not support a causal conclusion.

options.text: Using a short-answer test as the final measure
options.why: The type of test does not by itself support a causal conclusion.

options.text: Testing all students on the same day
options.why: Testing on the same day controls timing but does not make the groups comparable at the start.

options.text: Random assignment of students to the quiz and reread conditions
options.why: Random assignment makes the groups comparable at the start.
